Keyrook brand

One look for every Keyrook product — Keyrook Authenticator, the website, and the apps after it. Everything on this page is generated from packages/brand/src; the files it shows are in packages/brand/assets, and packages/brand/brand.css gives any page the same colours and movements.

The crow

A rook is two things: the chess piece the name suggests, and a bird of the crow family. Crows are known for picking things up and keeping them. Ours keeps a key. Its feathers are four crayons — the colours the product has always had — and its eye is the same yellow as the key.

Keyrook is drawn by hand: ink on paper, crayon colour, lines that wobble a little. It is plain and a bit rough on purpose. A security product that looks like a person made it is easier to trust than one that looks like a vault door.

Logo

On paper — the default

Two drawings, by size

Below 32 px the compact crow is used: no feet, two broad feathers, a bigger key. At 16 px a foot is a fifth of a pixel and four feathers are one smudge. markFor(px) picks the right one.

Room and size

  • Clear space round the crow: at least the width of the key on every side.
  • Smallest: the crow at 16 px (compact), the lockup at 120 px wide. Below that, use the crow alone.
  • The wordmark is lettered, not typed. Never set "keyrook" in a font to stand in for it.

Don't

Recolour the crow
Stretch it
Use Google's colours
Busy ground, no sticker

The family

The crow is Keyrook's, and only Keyrook's. It appears where the brand itself speaks: the Keyrook account every product signs in to, the emails it sends, Keyrook's own site, and a small "by Keyrook" at the foot of a product's page. A product never wears it as its icon.

Each product has its own mark, drawn in the same hand with the same four crayons, so the family shows without one member borrowing another's face. Its name is Keyrook and what it does.

Keyrook — the brand
Keyrook Authenticator
The next product — its own mark

Keyrook Authenticator

The countdown asterisk the extension has always had — eight ticks round a centre, like the dial of the 30-second timer every code runs on, and like the asterisks that mask a password — redrawn by hand in Keyrook's crayons. They run blue, yellow, red, green clockwise from twelve — warm pair together, cool pair together: neither Google's order, in either direction, nor Google's colours, which is what keeps eight coloured ticks from reading as theirs. Below 32 px the compact drawing, straighter and thicker. authenticatorMarkFor(px) picks it.

Type

Keyrook has no handwriting font. The hand shows in what is drawn — the crow, the wordmark, lines and boxes. Words stay in the system's own faces, so all fifty languages look like one product, and none falls back to a stranger's font halfway through a sentence.

TextThe quick brown fox — Chữ tiếng Việt — 日本語 — العربية
Codes482 913

--kr-font-sans, --kr-font-mono. Codes, addresses and recovery keys are mono, straight and still: a person reads them and types them somewhere else.

The scale

For sites and apps. Each step is a class in brand.css; line heights are even, so text sits on the 4 px beat. The code styles are tabular and always left to right. Tightening is dropped for Arabic, CJK and Thai, and a Vietnamese display heading gets room for a tone stacked on a hat.

.kr-display64/68 · 600 · -0.025emKeep the key
.kr-h144/52 · 600 · -0.02emMove to a new phone
.kr-h232/40 · 600 · -0.015emSync the server can't read
.kr-h324/32 · 600 · -0.01emYour recovery key
.kr-h419/28 · 600Last backed up yesterday at 21:04
.kr-body-lg19/30 · 400Every code is sealed on this device before it leaves. The server keeps closed boxes and no key.
.kr-body16/26 · 400Scan the QR code on the page you have open, or paste the secret. The account appears with a six-digit code that changes every 30 seconds.
.kr-small14/22 · 400Last signed in on Chrome, Mac, two hours ago.
.kr-caption12/18 · 500 · 0.01emCaptions, labels, footers. Never smaller than 12.
.kr-code-xl40/48 · 600 · 0.08em482 913
.kr-code28/36 · 600 · 0.06em073 518
.kr-code-sm15/24 · 500 · 0.02emK7QF-2MXA-9P4D-HT3R
  • Sentence case everywhere — headings, buttons, menus. Never all capitals: half the languages the product speaks have no capitals.
  • Two weights, 400 and 600. Emphasis is 600 or a crayon underline, not italics.
  • Lines of 45–75 Latin characters, 25–40 CJK. Buttons and labels grow with their words; design with the longest language.

Lettering

The wordmark's hand, carried on to the whole lower-case alphabet, the digits and the Vietnamese marks. It is drawn, not typed — there is no font file: letter(text) lays the strokes out as a mark, on the wordmark's grid and in its pen, and markSvg writes it with the words as its spoken title.

Drawn in the order a hand writes it — .kr-draw .kr-draw-in-turn
  • Display words only: 40 px and up, five words at most, one lettered phrase a screen. letter() refuses more.
  • Latin and Vietnamese only. A page in any other script sets the same words in its own face at display size, with a crayon underline: the hand is still there.
  • Never in an interface, and never for a code, an amount, a date or anything a person copies.
  • Never "keyrook": that is the wordmark, drawn on its own. letter() refuses it.
  • Ink, or paper on night. One word may take blue, red or green at 500 from 48 px; yellow is for underlines, never letters.

Lines and boxes

Three pen weights for drawn things — --kr-line-hair 1.5px, --kr-line-pen 2px, --kr-line-marker 3px at a 24 px icon. A box is drawn by hand with .kr-sketch: four corners that are not quite the same.

A card drawn by hand.
Its neighbour, turned round: .kr-sketch-alt.

Dense lists and tables keep a straight 1 px --kr-line: twenty wobbly lines in a row are noise. Drawn lines are for breaks between sections, one or two a screen. No paper texture: the paper colour is enough, and it prints clean.

Space and height

A 4 px beat under everything. The hand is in the lines; the measuring is here, so a drawn interface still lines up and is easy to hit — nothing a finger presses is smaller than 44 × 44.

Height is cut paper laid on the page: an ink line and a hard shadow down and to the right, never a blur.

.kr-raised — menus, toasts
.kr-floating — dialogs, sheets, with the page dimmed under ink at 40%

Icons

86 icons, drawn in the same pen on a 24-unit grid with a 20-unit live area. The hand is light, because an icon has to read in half a second at 16 px: a long line sags a little, corners are not all alike, a closed shape closes a touch past where it began. One colour — currentColor — and no fills but dots. Named for what they do, not what they show.

  • iconSvg('copy', { size: 20 }) writes one with its line set for the size (16 px → 1.5, 20 px → 1.75, 24 px → 2, 32 px → 2.5, 48 px → 3); or class="kr-icon kr-icon-20" on any of assets/icons/*.svg, or <use href="keyrook-icons.svg#kr-copy">.
  • An icon moves only when its meaning changes (copy → copied: the old one fades, the tick is drawn) or when it says something is under way (sync: its arrows are drawn again). It never spins.
  • Arrows and chevrons take .kr-icon-flip and point the way a right-to-left page reads.
  • Other companies' logos are never redrawn in this hand. They come compiled, as their owners drew them, from licensed sets; with none, the service's first letter on a neutral tile.

Motion

Two movements belong to Keyrook, both from hand-drawn animation, and the plain ones under them.

Draw — a line drawn in by the pen, once
Boil — redrawn a hair out of place, a few times, then still
fast120msa press, a toggle
base200msa sheet opening, a toast
slow400msa screen arriving
draw700msa line drawn in
boil150ms × 3, 4 roundsa drawing settling in
easecubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
  • Drawings move; text a person must read never does. A code that wobbles is a code read wrong.
  • Movement is brief and on arrival. Nothing loops forever except where something is genuinely waiting.
  • Only transform and opacity: nothing that moves the layout round it.
  • prefers-reduced-motion stops all of it. brand.css already does.

The plain ones

stagger40msbetween the items of a list arriving; six at most, the rest with the sixth
wait300msbefore anything says it is waiting — an indicator that flashes and vanishes is worse than none
hold1500mshow long "Copied" stays
toast4000mshow long a toast stays, a second more for every ten words
ease-incubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0) — leaving, in about two thirds of the time it took to arrive
ease-in-outcubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) — something on screen moving between two places
settlecubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1) — a small drawn thing landing like a stamp; never a block of text
linearthe 30-second countdown, and nothing else: time is linear
.kr-stagger — a list arriving
.kr-pop — landing like a stamp
can't read it.kr-highlight — crayon behind a word
.kr-wait — in place of a spinner
.kr-arrive, .kr-staggerup 8 px out of nothing: a screen, a section, a list
.kr-appearshown in place — a new code fades in where the old one stood; codes never slide, flip or count
.kr-leavegoing: a fade, quicker than coming
.kr-popa tick, a badge, a stamp landing
.kr-pressanything pressed: down at once, back with a little give
.kr-highlightcrayon laid behind a word, after the word has landed
.kr-draw-in-turnwith .kr-draw: the strokes one after another — the wordmark, lettering
.kr-waiton the Authenticator mark: its ticks light in turn while something is being waited on
.kr-blinkon the crow: one blink, two seconds after its page settles — Keyrook's own pages only

A wrong password does not shake the field: the text inside would shake with it. A hand-drawn outline is drawn round the field in red and boils once, and the message fades in under it.

Words

  • Keyrook is the brand, and names only what Keyrook products share: the account ("a Keyrook account"), the email sender.
  • Each product is Keyrook + what it does: Keyrook Authenticator. The name is never translated.
  • Plain and honest about limits. No "military-grade", no "unhackable".
  • Every word a person reads lives in a language file, the same keys in every language, so all languages say the same thing.

Using it

In a product in this repository:

import { markFor, markSvg, iconSvg, letter, CRAYON, MOTION } from '@keyrook/brand';
@import '…/packages/brand/brand.css';   /* --kr-* tokens, the type scale, .kr-icon, and every motion on this page */

Anywhere else — keyrook.com copies the kit with its own npm run brand — the files in packages/brand/assets (the icons are in assets/icons and assets/keyrook-icons.svg), brand.css, and the values on this page. Everything in brand.css is a class, so a page that allows one stylesheet and no inline styles can use all of it.
